newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain farmers estimate flood losses at 150 bln pta.
newsitem.headline: Spain farmers estimate flood losses at 150 bln pta.

text.p: Torrential rains in Spain have caused devastating damage in the southern region of Andalusia valued at around 150 billion pesetas, farmers' association ASAJA said on Friday.
"The worst hit region is Andalusia, where crop and structural damage has been catastrophic," the association said in a statement.
A breakdown of estimated damage reveals that crop damage is valued at some 106 billion pesetas, while structural damage is seen at 43 billion pesetas.
"In the presence of such severe damage the government must arrange the necessary measures to cushion the blow of economic losses for producers," the association said.
In the rest of Spain, other regions badly hit by heavy rains and snow include Extremadura, Castille La Mancha and Castille Leon.

The association said the principal crops affected included citric fruits, strawberries and flowers and more than 20 percent of the olive harvest has been destroyed. Torrential rains also damaged winter cereals, sugar beet, potatoes and horticultural products.
In addition, high winds and wet weather have harmed crops while flooding of pastures have increased cattle feed costs.

In La Mancha region, the association said almost a quarter of the olive crop had been lost. Storms had also severely delayed sowing in the region which could lead to a reduction in cereal crops this year.
In Castille Leon, sugar beet has been worst hit with almost 30 percent or 1.25 million tonnes still to be harvested.
"Production worth some 12 billion pesetas could be lost if the situation continues," the association said. --Madrid newsroom + 34 1 585 2161
